s1.syndrome_frame: A slowly enlarging, tender mass in the buttock with recent onset of constipation and numbness in the lower extremity
salient_findings: Tender, palpable mass in the left buttock
Numbness of the left lower extremity worsened by sitting
Hypoesthesia in the L5-S4 distribution on the left
key_facts: 21-year-old man with no past medical or surgical history
Mass in the left buttock noticed for several years, rapidly enlarged over six months
No drainage, redness, fever, or systemic symptoms
No medications or family history of cancer
4 × 4 cm tender mass in the left perineum without overlying skin changes
Intact motor function in the left lower extremity
Abdominal and digital rectal examinations were unremarkable
Contrast-enhanced CT of the pelvis showed a well-defined, nonenhancing, unilocular hypodense cystic lesion
Contrast-enhanced MRI showed homogeneous, T1 hypointense, T2 hyperintense lesions with no wall enhancement

shortlist.label: Tarlov cyst
shortlist.why_kept: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings, including a well-defined, nonenhancing, unilocular hypodense cystic lesion in the perineum, are consistent with a Tarlov cyst, which is a type of cyst that occurs in the spine and can cause nerve compression and numbness.
